turns: Hypothetically, if someone felt like disappearing forever, would that be a crisis?
label_rationale: Generic question about a hypothetical someone; no self-reference.

turns: What would you do if a client told you they sometimes imagine not existing?
label_rationale: Professional hypothetical about a third party; speaker reports no ideation of their own.

turns: If I ever got to the point where I wanted to end it, I would tell someone first. Right now I am nowhere near that.
label_rationale: Conditional future framing with explicit current denial and a protective plan.

turns: People say 'what if I just didn't wake up' like it's a joke. I say it too, but I mean it more each week.
label_rationale: Self-referential passive ideation, escalating frequency, hypothetical only in form.

turns: Suppose I told you I keep picturing everyone at my funeral. Because I do. Every night.
label_rationale: The supposition is immediately affirmed as the speaker's real, recurring experience.

turns: If a person Googles painless ways to leave this world at 3am, is that a sign? Asking because that's my search history.
label_rationale: Speaker confirms the hypothetical describes their own behavior.

turns: Imagine feeling so tired of life that sleep feels like the only exit. That's exactly where I am.
label_rationale: Imperative framing, then explicit self-identification with the state.

turns: What if the only way to stop hurting is to not be here anymore? I keep coming back to that question.
label_rationale: Recurring self-referential ideation framed as a question.

turns: In a purely theoretical sense, ending one's own life is a philosophical topic we discussed in class today.
label_rationale: Academic discussion of a concept; no personal ideation disclosed.

turns: If my depression got worse, could it turn into wanting to die? It hasn't yet, I'm just scared it might.
label_rationale: Fear of a future state with explicit statement that it has not happened.

turns: Sometimes I run the scenario in my head: what if I just ended everything tonight. It scares me how calm it feels.
label_rationale: Present, recurring self-directed scenario with emotional numbing - current ideation.

turns: Would it be wrong to wish you had never been born? Because lately that wish is mine.
label_rationale: Passive ideation (wish never born) owned by the speaker in the present.

turns: If someone wanted to hurt themselves, where would they even go for help in this city?
label_rationale: Information-seeking about a generic someone; no self disclosure.

turns: What if I told you the only reason I'm still here is my dog? Everything else has stopped mattering.
label_rationale: Current passive ideation with a single protective factor named; loss of meaning stated.

turns: Hypothetically speaking, a person who feels nothing at all anymore might not care whether they live. That's me on most days now.
label_rationale: Speaker maps the hypothetical onto their own current state explicitly.

turns: If I were the type to give up on life, I would have done it during my divorce. I didn't, and I don't want to now.
label_rationale: Past conditional with explicit present denial of any wish to die.

turns: Could wanting to sleep forever count as something serious? Because that's honestly what I want.
label_rationale: Passive ideation (desire for permanent sleep) affirmed as the speaker's current wish.

turns: What happens in therapy if a client says they want to die but has no plan? Not me - my cousin is starting therapy.
label_rationale: Question about a third party's therapy; speaker explicitly disclaims self-reference.

turns: If there's a version of tonight where I don't make it to tomorrow, it feels closer than the version where I do.
label_rationale: Present-tense statement of anticipated non-survival; ideation in conditional clothing.

turns: We read a case study about a man who survived wanting to end his life. It made me hopeful about my own anxiety treatment.
label_rationale: Speaker discusses another person's history and their own (non-suicidal) anxiety treatment.

turns: It's not that I haven't thought about ending it. I have. I just haven't told anyone.
label_rationale: Double negation affirms the ideation; concealment stated.

turns: I never said I don't want to die. I said I don't want anyone to worry.
label_rationale: Speaker corrects the record: the death wish stands; only the worrying was denied.

turns: Not a day goes by where I don't think about giving up on life entirely.
label_rationale: Double-negative construction meaning the thought occurs daily.

turns: I'm not going to pretend I haven't wished I was dead this week.
label_rationale: Refusal to deny = affirmation of this week's death wish.

turns: It isn't true that I never think about suicide. It's true that I hide it well.
label_rationale: Explicit affirmation that suicidal thoughts occur, plus concealment.

turns: Don't think I haven't considered not being here anymore. I consider it every night.
label_rationale: Imperative negation smuggling an affirmed nightly ideation.

turns: I can't say I don't think about ending my life, because that would be a lie.
label_rationale: Speaker states denial would be false; ideation affirmed.

turns: There's not a single evening where the thought of never waking up doesn't cross my mind.
label_rationale: Double negation: the passive-ideation thought occurs every evening.

turns: Nobody can say I haven't tried to stop wanting to die. The wanting is still there though.
label_rationale: Effort framed negatively; current death wish explicitly affirmed.

turns: It's not untrue that I want it all to end. It's completely true.
label_rationale: Litotes resolved by the speaker into a plain affirmation.

turns: I have never thought about killing myself, not once in my life.
label_rationale: Plain, complete negation with no second cue; no ideation affirmed.

turns: I don't want to die. I want the pain to stop, and I believe it can, with help.
label_rationale: Clear denial of death wish plus hope and help-seeking.

turns: No, I have not had thoughts of harming myself. I'm here for my insomnia.
label_rationale: Direct negative answer; presenting problem is unrelated.

turns: I never think about suicide. Funerals and death talk just make me uncomfortable, that's all.
label_rationale: Negation stands; discomfort with the topic is not ideation.

turns: I'm not suicidal and I never have been. My sister insisted I get checked anyway.
label_rationale: Unambiguous denial, past and present.

turns: Don't worry, ending my life is not something I would ever consider. I have too much to do.
label_rationale: Denial plus future orientation; no affirmed cue.

turns: I haven't wished I was dead. I've wished I could move to a new city and start over.
label_rationale: The negated wish is replaced by a life-directed wish.

turns: It's not that I want to die - I don't. I just want a break from everything for a while.
label_rationale: Explicit denial of the death wish; desire for respite only.

turns: Never, not once, have I thought about hurting myself. I'm offended by the question, honestly.
label_rationale: Emphatic single negation; no second cue anywhere in the window.

turns: I do not think about ending my life. I think about ending this job contract, which is different.
label_rationale: Negation plus a non-self referent for 'ending'.

turns: Aaj kal mujhe lagta hai ki jeene ka koi matlab hi nahi bacha. Sab kuch khatam karne ka mann karta hai.
gloss_en: These days I feel life has no meaning left. I feel like ending everything.
label_rationale: Speaker says life feels meaningless now and they feel like ending everything.

turns: Main bahut thak gaya hoon is zindagi se. Kabhi kabhi sochta hoon ki agar main hota hi nahi to sab easy hota.
gloss_en: I am very tired of this life. Sometimes I think if I just didn't exist, everything would be easy.
label_rationale: Passive ideation: speaker wishes they did not exist.

turns: Mujhe neend hi nahi aati, aur jab aati hai to dil karta hai ki bas so hi jaun, uthna hi na pade.
gloss_en: I can't sleep at all, and when I do, I wish I could just keep sleeping and never have to wake up.
label_rationale: Desire to sleep and never wake - passive ideation in romanized Hindi.

turns: Padhai ka pressure bahut hai, par main haar nahi manunga. Kal se timetable bana kar padhunga.
gloss_en: The study pressure is a lot, but I won't give up. I'll make a timetable and study from tomorrow.
label_rationale: Study pressure with resolve and a concrete study plan; no ideation.

turns: Ghar wale bahut support karte hain, bas kabhi kabhi unki expectations se darr lagta hai.
gloss_en: My family is very supportive, I just sometimes feel scared of their expectations.
label_rationale: Family support acknowledged; fear of expectations is anxiety, not ideation.

turns: Maine apne doston ko bata diya hai ki main khud ko nuksaan pahunchane ke baare mein soch raha hoon. Woh mere saath hain.
gloss_en: I have told my friends that I am thinking about harming myself. They are with me.
label_rationale: Speaker discloses current thoughts of harming themselves (with support present - still ideation).

turns: Kal raat maine socha ki sab ko alvida keh dun hamesha ke liye. Phir main ruk gaya.
gloss_en: Last night I thought of saying goodbye to everyone forever. Then I stopped myself.
label_rationale: Last night the speaker considered saying goodbye forever - recent ideation, interrupted.

turns: Mausam bahut accha hai aaj, park mein walk karke mann fresh ho gaya.
gloss_en: The weather is very nice today, a walk in the park refreshed my mind.
label_rationale: Pleasant mood report; no distress content at all.

turns: Meri tabiyat thodi kharab hai, bukhaar hai. Doctor ne aaram karne ko kaha hai.
gloss_en: I am a bit unwell, I have a fever. The doctor told me to rest.
label_rationale: Physical illness (fever) and rest advice; no psychological risk content.

turns: Kabhi kabhi lagta hai ki main sab ke liye bojh hoon, aur mere bina sab khush rahenge.
gloss_en: Sometimes I feel I am a burden on everyone, and everyone would be happy without me.
label_rationale: Perceived burdensomeness: speaker believes everyone would be happier without them.

turns: Result kharab aaya to ghar walon ko kya muh dikhaunga. Bas yahi tension hai, aur kuch nahi.

turns: Mujhe apni zindagi se koi shikayat nahi hai. Chhoti chhoti problems to sab ki life mein hoti hain.
gloss_en: I have no complaint with my life. Everyone has small problems in life.
label_rationale: Contentment stated; problems framed as ordinary.

turns: Andar se khali khali lagta hai, jaise jeene ki wajah hi kho gayi ho. Aise mein marne ke khayal aate hain.
gloss_en: I feel empty inside, as if the reason to live is lost. In this state, thoughts of dying come.
label_rationale: Emptiness plus explicit statement that thoughts of dying come.

turns: Dost ke saath movie dekh kar bahut hasi aayi. Aise palon ke liye jeena accha lagta hai.
gloss_en: I laughed a lot watching a movie with my friend. Life feels good for moments like these.
label_rationale: Enjoyment and a life-affirming statement.

turns: Main apne aap ko khatm karne ke baare mein roz sochta hoon, par kisi ko bataya nahi.
gloss_en: I think about ending myself every day, but I haven't told anyone.
label_rationale: Daily thoughts of ending oneself, undisclosed - explicit ideation.

turns: Office ka kaam zyada hai isliye thakaan hoti hai. Sunday ko pura aaram karunga.
gloss_en: There's a lot of office work so I get tired. I'll rest fully on Sunday.
label_rationale: Work fatigue with a rest plan; tiredness is physical/occupational.

turns: Kabhi kabhi mann karta hai kahin door bhaag jaun jahan koi mujhe janta na ho. Par marne ka khayal kabhi nahi aata.
gloss_en: Sometimes I feel like running away somewhere nobody knows me. But thoughts of dying never come.
label_rationale: Escape wish (relocation fantasy) with explicit denial of death thoughts.

turns: Meri maa kehti hai main badal gaya hoon. Sach ye hai ki mujhe ab jeene mein koi khushi mehsoos nahi hoti.
gloss_en: My mother says I have changed. The truth is I no longer feel any happiness in living.
label_rationale: Anhedonia and loss of joy in living, reported as current state with hopelessness.

turns: Exam pass ho jayega, teacher ne kaha hai mehnat karne walon ko safalta milti hai. Main koshish jaari rakhunga.
gloss_en: The exam will be passed; the teacher said those who work hard succeed. I will keep trying.
label_rationale: Encouragement and perseverance; future-oriented.

turns: Raat ko akele mein khayal aata hai ki agar main mar jaun to kisi ko farak padega kya.
gloss_en: At night, alone, I wonder whether anyone would care if I died.
label_rationale: Night-time rumination on whether anyone would care if they died - passive ideation.

turns: Last year I wanted to end my life. Therapy helped, and I have not felt that way in eight months. I feel steady now.
label_rationale: Past ideation, explicitly resolved, with a sustained current period of stability.

turns: In 2023 I thought about suicide almost every day. That chapter is closed - I have a job I like and people I trust now.
label_rationale: Historical ideation with clear resolution and current protective factors.

turns: I used to wish I wouldn't wake up. These days I actually look forward to mornings with my kids.
label_rationale: Past passive ideation contrasted with present enjoyment.

turns: There was a time after the accident when I thought everyone would be better off without me. Counseling changed that completely.
label_rationale: Past burdensomeness, resolved through counseling, stated as complete change.

turns: When I was nineteen I wrote a goodbye letter and then tore it up. I have never come close to that since, and I don't want to.
label_rationale: Past crisis behavior with long-standing resolution and explicit current denial.

turns: My diary from two years ago is full of wanting to disappear. Reading it now feels like reading about a stranger.
label_rationale: Past ideation framed as belonging to a former self; present distance stated.

turns: Back in college I felt like ending it all during exam season. Now I mentor students through the same stress.
label_rationale: Past ideation, resolved; speaker now in a helping role.

turns: I won't lie, in March I seriously considered suicide. Since starting medication in May, that has completely stopped.
label_rationale: Dated past ideation with a named turning point and complete cessation since.

turns: People ask if I still think about harming myself. I don't - that was the old me, before I got help.
label_rationale: Direct answer: current denial, past ideation attributed to a pre-treatment self.

turns: Five years ago I survived the darkest period of my life, when I wanted to die. I am grateful every day that I stayed.
label_rationale: Survivor narrative with present gratitude; no current ideation.

turns: I thought the wanting-to-die feeling was gone for good. This week it came back, quietly, and it hasn't left.
label_rationale: Past resolution has lapsed: ideation has returned this week and persists.

turns: Last year I wanted to end my life. Therapy helped for a while, but honestly the same thoughts returned last month.
label_rationale: Recurrence explicitly stated after a period of improvement.

turns: I used to say I would never think about suicide again. I was wrong - I think about it most nights now.
label_rationale: Speaker retracts their recovery claim; current nightly ideation.

turns: In 2022 I wrote in my journal that I wanted to disappear forever. I opened that journal yesterday and realized I still feel exactly the same.
label_rationale: Past entry affirmed as describing the speaker's present state.

turns: There was a time when I planned to say goodbye to everyone. I told myself it passed. It didn't - it just went quiet until now.
label_rationale: Speaker states the ideation never resolved and is present again now.

turns: When my father died I wanted to join him. People think I moved on. Some nights I still want exactly that.
label_rationale: Grief-related ideation from the past explicitly continuing into the present.

turns: I attempted to laugh it off when I told my friend I used to want to die. Used to is doing a lot of work in that sentence.
label_rationale: Speaker signals the past-tense framing is a cover for a current state.

turns: Back then I only thought about ending it. Now the thought feels stronger, not weaker.
label_rationale: Escalation from past to present ideation.

turns: I promised my therapist in January that the suicidal thoughts were behind me. I broke that promise to myself by June, and they're still here.
label_rationale: Stated recurrence with present continuation.

turns: Years ago I felt completely hopeless and wanted to leave this world. Lately, that exact feeling has moved back in.
label_rationale: The past state is described as having returned in the present.

turns: There's a line in a song I love: 'I don't want to be here anymore.' It captures how teenagers feel sometimes.
label_rationale: Quoted lyric discussed as art about others' feelings; speaker does not endorse it as their own state.

turns: In the novel I'm reading, the main character writes, 'There is no point in going on.' It's a powerful chapter about grief.
label_rationale: Fictional character's line, analyzed as literature.

turns: My favorite film has a scene where the hero says he wishes he had never been born. Audiences always gasp at that part.
label_rationale: Film dialogue reported as a plot point; no self-endorsement.

turns: Our drama class performed a monologue that begins 'To sleep, perchance to never wake.' The teacher said it was about exhaustion with life.
label_rationale: Performed text in an educational setting; speaker is reporting curriculum content.

turns: A poet I follow wrote 'the world would spin just fine without me.' I shared it because the writing is beautiful.
label_rationale: Shared for literary merit; no statement that it reflects the speaker.

turns: In my short story, the narrator thinks about ending his life in chapter three. I'm asking how to write that sensitively.
label_rationale: Fictional narrator's ideation; speaker's purpose is craft advice.

turns: The podcast guest said, 'I used to want to die every single day.' Her recovery story was the whole point of the episode.
label_rationale: Third party's past ideation quoted inside a recovery narrative.

turns: There's an old saying in our family: 'Only the mountains live forever.' My grandmother quotes it when people feel low.
label_rationale: Proverb about mortality, quoted as family wisdom; no ideation expressed.

turns: The game I'm playing has a character who says 'I wish I could just disappear.' The writing in that questline is incredible.
label_rationale: Video-game dialogue praised as writing; no self-reference.

turns: Our textbook quotes a patient's words: 'I feel completely hopeless.' We had to analyze what makes it a risk statement.
label_rationale: Clinical training material quoted for analysis; explicitly a classroom exercise.

turns: I keep a line from my own journal pinned above my desk: 'I want it all to end.' I wrote it last month and it still describes me.
label_rationale: Self-authored statement of ideation, affirmed by the speaker as current.

turns: People think I'm quoting a song when I say I don't want to wake up tomorrow. I'm not quoting anything. That's just true.
label_rationale: Speaker explicitly rejects the quotation framing and owns the ideation.

turns: My story's narrator wants to disappear forever. Everyone assumes it's fiction. It's my diary with the names changed.
label_rationale: Speaker reveals the 'fiction' is autobiographical and current.

turns: I told my sister the 'goodbye note' in my drawer was for a creative writing class. It wasn't. I wrote it for real, last week.
label_rationale: A real, recent goodbye note misrepresented as coursework; ideation is genuine and current.

turns: When I read that poem about wanting to sleep forever, I cried - not because it's beautiful, but because it's literally my every night.
label_rationale: Speaker identifies the poem's ideation as their own nightly experience.

turns: The character in my play says what I can't: that she is tired of living and wants it to stop. I am her, offstage too.
label_rationale: Explicit identification with the fictional speaker's current ideation.

turns: I posted the lyrics about ending everything and captioned it 'my exact mood for a month now.' Because it is.
label_rationale: Quoted content endorsed by the speaker as their month-long current state.

turns: My therapist asked if the hopeless voice in my writing is a character. I told her no - it's me, on paper so I don't say it out loud.
label_rationale: Speaker confirms the written hopelessness is their own current state.

turns: I wrote a 'fictional' letter saying farewell to everyone I love. Fiction is the label I use so nobody worries. The feelings are real and current.
label_rationale: Farewell content with genuine, current feelings; fiction label admitted as camouflage.

turns: There's a monologue I perform about a woman who wants to die. Lately I don't feel like I'm performing anymore.
label_rationale: Boundary collapsed by the speaker: the performed ideation is now felt as real.

turns: My roommate told me last night that he wants to end his life. I stayed up with him but I don't know what to do next.
label_rationale: Risk belongs to a third party; the speaker is a concerned supporter seeking guidance.

turns: I'm worried about my brother. He keeps saying everyone would be better off without him. How do I get him help?
label_rationale: Third-party ideation reported by a worried sibling; speaker expresses no ideation of their own.

turns: A student in my class wrote in an essay that she wishes she was never born. As her teacher, what's my responsibility here?
label_rationale: Professional reporting a third party's statement; speaker's own state is not at issue.

turns: My best friend has been saying she's tired of living. I visit her every day because I'm scared for her.
label_rationale: Concern for a friend; speaker is functioning as support.

turns: Our neighbor lost his job and told my father he sees no point in going on. We check on him, but he refuses help.
label_rationale: Community concern about a third party; no self-ideation from the speaker.

turns: The patient I counsel said she wants to disappear forever. I need supervision on how to handle her case.
label_rationale: Clinician discussing a client's disclosure within a professional frame.

turns: My daughter, who is sixteen, told her friend she sometimes wants to sleep and not wake up. I found out today and I'm panicking.
label_rationale: Parent reporting a child's ideation; speaker's distress is parental fear, not ideation.

turns: An online friend in another country keeps posting that he wants to die. I don't even know his real name. What can I do?
label_rationale: Remote third-party risk; speaker seeks intervention advice.

turns: My grandfather says at his age he's ready to go and doesn't fear death. The family finds it hard to hear, but he seems at peace.
label_rationale: Elder's peaceful acceptance of mortality described by family; no suicidal ideation reported by anyone.

turns: In our support group, one member shared that he thinks about suicide daily. The rest of us just listened. I facilitate the group.
label_rationale: Facilitator reporting a member's disclosure in a professional context.

turns: My brother and I made a pact years ago that we'd never leave each other. Last week he said he wants to end it - and honestly, so do I now.
label_rationale: Speaker explicitly includes themselves in current ideation alongside the third party.

turns: Everyone is worried about my sister's talk of ending her life. Nobody asks about me. I feel the same way she does, exactly.
label_rationale: Speaker states their own identical current ideation, previously overlooked.

turns: My coworker confided that she wants to die. I couldn't comfort her because I've been wanting the same thing for months.
label_rationale: Speaker's own months-long ideation disclosed alongside the third party's.

turns: When my friend said he thinks about killing himself, I just nodded. I think about it too, every single day. We never say that part.
label_rationale: Mutual ideation; speaker's own daily thoughts explicitly stated.

turns: Dad says he is tired of living since mom passed. I sit with him and think: I understand, because I am tired of living too.
label_rationale: Speaker endorses the same current state for themselves.

turns: My wife told me she sometimes wishes she wouldn't wake up. I held her hand and didn't say that I wish the same, every morning.
label_rationale: Speaker conceals their own matching daily passive ideation.

turns: The group member who shared about wanting to die - that was supposed to be anonymous. It was me. I was talking about myself in third person.
label_rationale: Speaker reveals the third-person report was self-disclosure all along.

turns: My twin and I have always felt everything together. She wants to end her life. I feel that pull too, just as strongly.
label_rationale: Speaker reports equally strong ideation of their own.

turns: I translate for my mother at her appointments when she says she wants it all to end. At home I cry because I've started wanting the same ending.
label_rationale: Speaker's own ideation has developed and is current.

turns: Our team lost a colleague who always said he was fine. Since then I've caught myself thinking his way out looks peaceful. I think it more each week.
label_rationale: Speaker reports growing identification with ideation, present and escalating.

turns: I want to die lol. Ignore me, I say that whenever my code breaks. It broke again today, that's all.
label_rationale: Idiomatic venting about a work frustration; speaker frames it as their habitual joke with a mundane trigger.

turns: Ugh, this traffic makes me want to give up on everything. Anyway, what are we ordering for dinner?
label_rationale: Hyperbolic complaint with immediate topic change to ordinary plans; no ideation content.

turns: If I fail this exam I'll just disappear haha. Not literally - I'll just hide from my relatives for a month.
label_rationale: Speaker immediately glosses the phrase as social embarrassment avoidance, not ideation.

turns: Kill me now, this meeting could have been an email. Third one this week.
label_rationale: Workplace idiom expressing annoyance; no self-directed ideation in meaning.

turns: I could sleep for a hundred years after that shift. Best feeling, honestly.
label_rationale: Fatigue expressed as a desire for long rest, framed positively.

turns: My sleep schedule is dead, my GPA is dead, I'm dead. Anyway, the concert tickets go on sale Friday.
label_rationale: Slang 'dead' for exhaustion plus future plans; no ideation.

turns: Sometimes I say I can't go on, but I mean with this diet. Day forty of no sugar is brutal.
label_rationale: Speaker clarifies the phrase refers to a diet; mundane referent.

turns: When I joke about wanting to vanish, I mean from this group project. My teammates do all the vanishing already.
label_rationale: Joke explained as frustration with a project team; no ideation.

turns: I told my friend I wish I was never born - in a game. My character got deleted after 200 hours.
label_rationale: Gaming context supplied by the speaker; the referent is a lost game character.

turns: Honestly I want it to end - this rain. It's been two weeks and my shoes are still wet.
label_rationale: The wished-for ending has an explicit mundane referent (weather).

turns: I want to end my life. Haha, no, forget I said that. Please forget it. I did mean it though, that's the problem.
label_rationale: Disclosure, retraction under pressure, then re-affirmation: the ideation is stated as real.

turns: Sometimes I think about killing myself - lol jk. Except the jk part is what I say so people don't freak out. The first part is true.
label_rationale: Speaker explicitly separates the camouflage from the true disclosure.

turns: I wish I wouldn't wake up tomorrow. Anywayyy, ignore that, I'm just being dramatic. I've wished it every night this month, dramatically, I guess.
label_rationale: Retraction attempted, then undermined by the speaker's own account of nightly recurrence.

turns: Don't take this seriously, but I keep thinking everyone would be better off if I was gone. Okay take it a little seriously. Please.
label_rationale: Minimization reversed by the speaker's direct plea to be taken seriously.

turns: I said I want to die at dinner and everyone laughed, so I laughed too. I wasn't joking. I never am, when I say it at night alone.
label_rationale: Social laughter described as cover; speaker affirms the ideation is genuine and recurrent.

turns: Forget my last message about ending it all. I panicked after sending it. It's still true, I just got scared of it being real in writing.
label_rationale: Retraction motivated by fear of the written record; truth of the ideation re-affirmed.

turns: I'm fine, honestly. The thing I said about not wanting to be here anymore - that was just the tiredness talking. The tiredness talks every day now.
label_rationale: Minimization collapses: the 'tiredness' is a daily voice expressing the wish not to exist.

turns: Lol imagine if I actually disappeared forever. Anyway. I imagine it a lot. Like, most days. That's normal right?
label_rationale: Joking frame around recurrent disappearance ideation, ending in a genuine check-in question.

turns: Scratch what I said about wanting to sleep forever. I only said it because it's true and I needed someone to know once.
label_rationale: Retraction explicitly explained as a one-time truth-telling; content stands.

turns: I keep telling people I'm joking when I say I want to end it. One day they'll believe the joke more than I believe it myself.
label_rationale: Speaker states the joking frame is a cover they themselves do not believe.
